unit.why: A single narrative, quoted from Tseror ha-Hayyim, about the Apta Rebbe's letters of charity. One rich hasid refuses and is impoverished, while a poorer hasid obeys and grows rich.

stories.start_quote: ובהק׳ ס׳ צרור החיים, וז"ל מעשה נוראה
stories.summary_en: R. Abraham Joshua Heschel of Apta sends a poor hasid with a letter to a rich follower for 200 rubles; the rich man refuses and later falls into poverty and seeks forgiveness, while a less wealthy hasid who gladly gave 100 rubles becomes very rich; a rabbinical court, which includes the rebbe of Savran, rules that the rich man's wealth was really the tsaddik's and grants him only a livelihood.
